description: Expected evaluated state of reference.json at the five golden timestamps (specification §3.3). Pure data, derived by hand from the rule below and never generated from an implementation: the runtime is tested against these numbers, not the other way round. Each `state` is exactly what `evaluateComposition(reference, timeUs)` of @kadrion/runtime must return, compared bit for bit. Derived first in PR-02 for identity base values and again in PR-03, when the project owner gave the reference composition base values that are not the identity (D18).
rule: Shape: the state mirrors the document. Scenes, nodes, and group children keep their order and hierarchy (D16.4), and every value is local to the node's parent (D15). The background has no transform.
A property without an animation keeps its base value.

Lifetime (D42.2, D42.3): a node is active at t when t >= startUs and t - startUs < durationUs. Every node of the reference composition, the background and the children of the group included, has startUs 0 and durationUs 10 000 000, the duration of the composition, so every node state says active: true at every golden timestamp. active is local to its node.

Sampling (D16.6): at or before the first keyframe the first value holds; at or after the last keyframe the last value holds; a time exactly on a keyframe yields that keyframe's value without any arithmetic.

Interpolation (D18): strictly between the keyframes (t0, a) and (t1, b), each scalar channel is a + ((b - a) * (t - t0)) / (t1 - t0), evaluated in exactly this order in IEEE 754 binary64. x and y are independent channels.
Composition with the base value (D16.6), one operation: position = base + offset, scale = base * factor, opacity = base * factor.

Animations of the reference composition: node-group position offsets (16, 8) at 0 and (76, 308) at 7 500 000 on the base (60, 420); node-image scale factors (1, 1) at 2 500 000 and (1.75, 1.375) at 10 000 000 on the base (1.25, 1.25); node-title opacity factors 0.25 at 0 and 1 at 7 500 000 on the base 0.75. node-caption and node-custom-html are not animated.
RN(v) below is the binary64 value nearest to v, ties to even.

derivation: node-group position: 0 is the first keyframe, so the offset is (16, 8) and the position is (60 + 16, 420 + 8) = (76, 428).
node-image scale: 0 lies before the first keyframe at 2 500 000, so the first factor (1, 1) holds and the scale is (1.25 * 1, 1.25 * 1) = (1.25, 1.25).
node-title opacity: 0 is the first keyframe, so the factor is 0.25 and the opacity is 0.75 * 0.25 = 0.1875. Exact: 0.75 = 3 * 2^-2 and 0.25 = 2^-2, so the product is 3 * 2^-4.
node-image scale: 2 500 000 is the first keyframe, so the factor is (1, 1) and the scale is (1.25 * 1, 1.25 * 1) = (1.25, 1.25).

node-title opacity: between 0 and 7 500 000. Factor = 0.25 + ((1 - 0.25) * 2 500 000) / 7 500 000 = 0.25 + 1 875 000 / 7 500 000 = 0.25 + 0.25 = 0.5. Opacity = 0.75 * 0.5 = 0.375. Every step is exact: all values are dyadic.
node-group position: 7 500 000 is the last keyframe, so the offset is (76, 308) and the position is (60 + 76, 420 + 308) = (136, 728).
node-title opacity: 7 500 000 is the last keyframe, so the factor is 1 and the opacity is 0.75 * 1 = 0.75.
node-group position: 9 900 000 lies after the last keyframe at 7 500 000, so the last offset (76, 308) holds and the position is (136, 728).

node-image scale: elapsed 7 400 000 of 7 500 000; the keyframe at 10 000 000 is never reached, because the composition end is exclusive (D16.5). Factor x = 1 + (0.75 * 7 400 000) / 7 500 000 = 1 + 5 550 000 / 7 500 000 = 1 + RN(0.74); factor y = 1 + (0.375 * 7 400 000) / 7 500 000 = 1 + 2 775 000 / 7 500 000 = 1 + RN(0.37). Both products are exact integers.

Scale x = 1.25 * 7 836 263 351 624 663 * 2^-52 = 39 181 316 758 123 315 * 2^-54 = 4 897 664 594 765 414.375 * 2^-51. The product lies in [2, 4), where the spacing is 2^-51, so it rounds down to 4 897 664 594 765 414 * 2^-51. The literal 2.175 is 2.175 * 2^51 = 4 897 664 594 765 414.4 * 2^-51 and rounds to the same value, so the expected x is the JSON number 2.175.

Scale y = 1.25 * 6 169 931 489 497 580 * 2^-52 = 7 712 414 361 871 975 * 2^-52 exactly (6 169 931 489 497 580 / 4 * 5). The product lies in [1, 2), where the spacing is 2^-52, and 7 712 414 361 871 975 < 2^53, so it is representable and the multiplication is exact. The literal 1.7125 is 1.7125 * 2^52 = 7 712 414 361 871 974.4 * 2^-52 and rounds to 7 712 414 361 871 974 * 2^-52: the expected y is one unit in the last place above RN(1.7125). Its shortest decimal is 1.7125000000000001: that literal is 1.7125 + 1e-16, while the neighbours lie 0.89e-16 below and 1.33e-16 and 3.55e-16 above 1.7125, so 7 712 414 361 871 975 * 2^-52 is the nearest, and 1.712500000000000 (16 digits) would read back as the lower neighbour.

Scale = (2.175, 1.7125000000000001). An evaluation that folded the base value into the keyframe endpoints would compute y = 1.25 + ((1.71875 - 1.25) * 7 400 000) / 7 500 000 = 1.25 + 3 468 750 / 7 500 000 = 1.25 + RN(0.4625); 0.4625 * 2^54 = 8 331 659 310 635 417.6 rounds to 8 331 659 310 635 418 * 2^-54 = 2 082 914 827 658 854.5 * 2^-52, and adding 1.25 = 5 629 499 534 213 120 * 2^-52 gives 7 712 414 361 871 974.5 * 2^-52, a tie that goes to the even 7 712 414 361 871 974 * 2^-52 = RN(1.7125). It would therefore miss the expected y by one unit in the last place; in x both routes happen to give 2.175.
node-title opacity: after the last keyframe, so the last factor 1 holds and the opacity is 0.75 * 1 = 0.75.
